title: Unit Conversion
description: Essential Criteria: The response must correctly convert the initial speed from 36 km/h to 10 m/s.

title: Acceleration Calculation
description: Essential Criteria: The response must correctly apply the average acceleration formula a = (v_f - v_i)/Δt, yielding approximately -8300 m/s².

title: Lethal Threshold
description: Essential Criteria: The response must correctly calculate the lethal acceleration threshold as 500g = 5000 m/s².

title: Comparison and Conclusion
description: Important Criteria: The response must compare the calculated acceleration magnitude (8300 m/s²) to the lethal threshold (5000 m/s²) and conclude the acceleration is life-threatening.

title: Sign Convention
description: Important Criteria: The response must correctly interpret the negative sign in acceleration as indicating deceleration/direction and compare magnitudes.

title: Physics Model Application
description: Optional Criteria: The response may explicitly state the assumption of constant acceleration and post-collision zero velocity as given in the problem.

title: Unit Consistency
description: Pitfall Criteria: Penalize if calculations mix units (e.g., km/h with m/s²) without proper conversion.

title: Sign Error in Comparison
description: Pitfall Criteria: Penalize if the conclusion is based on the signed acceleration value (-8300 < 5000) instead of comparing magnitudes.
